t: You have kept us this far. Keep us useful to one another.
Thank you for the work, the food, and everyone who came home.
Stay near this village. We are trying to make it worthy.
I ask for nothing today. I only wanted to give thanks.
Watch our hands and help us use what you have given well.
I think you heard us before. I hope you still do.
I came to speak, though I am still unsure who listens.
Maybe gratitude can come before certainty. Thank you for today.
I do not know whether you helped. I know we needed help.
Keep listening while I learn how to believe.
I am speaking because silence has answered nothing either.
If anyone hears this, I could use one honest sign.
I do not expect an answer. That does not stop the asking.
Perhaps I am talking to myself. I needed to say it anyway.
Show me that prayer is more than kneeling and waiting.
Thank you for the roof above us. Keep it strong.
You gave this household shelter. Let us share it well.
Bless these walls and everyone welcomed through the door.
Maybe you helped this roof rise. I am grateful either way.
The rain stays outside now. I thought somebody should hear my thanks.
I asked for shelter once. I am still deciding who answered.
Builders made this roof, but I will thank anyone else who helped.
I trust these beams more than prayer. Please prove me incomplete.
The roof is real. Whether you are real remains the question.
Hold the roofs down and guide everyone home through this storm.
Turn the worst wind aside. The village is in your hands.
Stay with the people outside until they reach a door.
If you can quiet the wind, now would be a kind time.
I do not know whether storms listen. I hope you do.
Help the roofs hold. I will decide what that means afterward.
The storm will pass by itself. I am asking you to surprise me.
Wind does not bargain, and I doubt gods do either.
If prayer changes weather, this is the moment to demonstrate it.
Watch every sleeping house until morning returns.
Keep wolves far and fires steady through the night.
Stay beside the watch while the rest of us sleep.
Night makes belief easier and doubt less comfortable.
If you are near, keep the dark outside our doors.
I will trust the guard and leave a little trust for you.
Darkness is only darkness. Still, I would rather not face it alone.
I know the watch keeps us safe. If you help, help them.
I doubt you hear this. Night gives me time to test the doubt.
The stores are empty. Put food where hungry hands can reach it.
You have fed us before. Please do not let us fail now.
Send enough for the children first and the workers after.
I trust you, but trust does not quiet an empty stomach.
Give us food, and we will use the strength to rebuild the stores.
Hear every hungry person in this village, not only me.
We have stretched every sack and scraped every pot. Please provide.
I came with faith and an empty belly. Answer whichever you notice first.
Judge the person who wronged me. I have waited long enough.
You know what they did. Let them answer for it.
Take their comfort until they understand what they caused.
I ask for justice, though anger may be choosing the punishment.
Do not let their good name hide what they did to me.
I should not ask this, but I want them to suffer.
Maybe justice is the word I use because revenge sounds ugly.
I came here angry. I am leaving the choice with you.
Part of me wants them struck. Part of me hopes you refuse.
If you punish them, I may regret asking. I am asking anyway.
Bless the road and the people willing to walk it.
Guide us to the new ground and bring every traveler through safely.
We will take your name beyond this town. Give us your blessing.
Keep our provisions sound and our path clear until the banner rises.
Watch the families leaving and the families staying behind.
Give us courage for the distance and sense enough to turn back if needed.
We have chosen the road. Walk it with us.
Let the new town begin with your favor and our honest work.
